h1: The 6 Best E-Readers With Audiobook Support of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best E-Readers With Audiobooks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six e-readers that play audiobooks, sorted by store support, Bluetooth, text to speech, speaker and display type.
summary: The Kobo Libra Colour is the best e-reader for audiobooks because it plays purchased audiobooks from its own store over Bluetooth. The PocketBook InkPad Color 3 is the pick if you want a built in speaker, and the Verse Pro Color is the compact color option. The OBOOK6 is the budget route for people willing to install their own audiobook apps.
intro: Shoppers often assume that any e-reader with Bluetooth plays audiobooks, but there are three very different paths. Some devices have a native audiobook store, some read your ebooks aloud with text to speech, and some run Android so you can install a third party app. Picking the wrong path is the most common buyer mistake in this category.

Six devices were assessed here, relying on spec sheets and what owners report about audio use. We ranked them on how directly they play audiobooks, Bluetooth and speaker options, storage, display type and value. Android devices with weaker audio claims and one duplicate color variant were left out.

products.name: Kobo Libra Colour, 7" Glare-Free Colour E Ink Kaleido 3, Waterproof, Black
products.verdict: The only pick here with a native audiobook store built in.
products.description:
The Kobo Libra Colour has a 7 inch glare free color E Ink Kaleido 3 display, supports Kobo audiobooks and pairs with Bluetooth headphones. It is also waterproof, which makes it a good bath or poolside reader.

It ranks first because audiobooks are a native feature rather than a workaround. You buy and play audio in the same place you buy ebooks, with no app juggling. The cost is the highest price bracket in this ranking, in the $200 to $500 band.

Buy it if you want one integrated library for both reading and listening. The caveat is that your audiobooks come from Kobo's store, so existing subscriptions elsewhere will not carry over.
products.idealFor: Readers wanting one library for ebooks and audio.
products.skipIf: You already subscribe to another audiobook service.

products.name: PocketBook InkPad Color 3, 7.8" Color E-Paper Display, Built-In Speaker
products.verdict: Plays audio out loud with no headphones, on a big 7.8 inch screen.
products.description:
The InkPad Color 3 has a 7.8 inch color E Paper display, a built in speaker, text to speech and Bluetooth. It is the largest screen in the roundup.

It ranks second because the built in speaker removes the headphones requirement, which is rare in this category. It falls behind the Kobo because there is no first party audiobook store named in the listing, so playback relies on text to speech and your own files.

It suits people who want to listen in the kitchen or car without extra gear. The speaker on a device this thin will not sound like a speaker system, so use Bluetooth for serious listening.
products.idealFor: Listeners who do not want headphones.
products.skipIf: You want a native audiobook store.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro Color, 6" E Ink Kaleido 3, Text-to-Speech & Bluetooth
products.verdict: A pocketable color reader with text to speech and IPX8 waterproofing.
products.description:
The Verse Pro Color has a 6 inch Kaleido 3 color E Ink screen, text to speech, Bluetooth and an IPX8 waterproof rating. It is the small, color version of the Verse Pro family.

It ranks third because it is cheaper than the two above it but leaves out a speaker and a native audiobook store. Text to speech reads any book aloud in a synthetic voice, which suits commutes but is not the same as a narrated audiobook.

Choose it for a compact color reader in the $100 to $200 range. If you want professional narration, you need the Kobo.
products.idealFor: Color readers wanting a compact body.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro E-Reader Waterproof, 6" E-Ink Carta HD, Azure
products.verdict: A waterproof black and white reader sold as an audiobook and ebook device.
products.description:
The Verse Pro has a 6 inch E Ink Carta HD screen, WiFi and Bluetooth, and 16GB of storage. The listing names it as both an audiobook and ebook reader, and it is waterproof.

It ranks fourth because the black and white screen skips the color of the Verse Pro Color above it. The extra 16GB of storage is generous for audio files, which are much larger than ebooks.

It suits buyers who want an affordable, waterproof, small device for audio and text and have no need for color.
products.idealFor: Affordable audio and text on a small body.

products.name: PocketBook Era Lite, Affordable 7" e-Reader, Bluetooth & Text-to-Speech Support
products.verdict: A large 7 inch reader with text to speech and up to two months of battery.
products.description:
The Era Lite has a 7 inch screen, Bluetooth, text to speech and up to 2 months of battery life. It is built to be an affordable large screen reader.

It ranks fifth because it lacks the waterproofing and extra storage of the Verse Pro and offers only text to speech for audio. In exchange you get the bigger display and long battery life.

Choose it if you read mostly and want occasional text to speech. If audiobooks are a priority, the models above give more.

products.name: OBOOK6 eReader (32GB), 6" 300ppi Glare-Free Display, Android
products.verdict: A cheap Android reader that lets you install your own audiobook apps.
products.description:
The OBOOK6 is a 6 inch, 300ppi glare free reader with 32GB of storage that runs Android. Because it runs genuine Android, it can use third party audiobook apps.

It ranks last because audio support depends on apps you install, rather than anything native. It is also the cheapest pick here, in the $50 to $100 range.

It is for budget buyers comfortable with Android who want to try an existing audiobook subscription on an e-reader.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with an existing audiobook app.
products.skipIf: You want everything to work out of the box.

whatMatters.detail: There are three ways an e-reader plays audio. A native store like Kobo's sells and plays audiobooks, text to speech reads any ebook aloud in a synthetic voice, and Android devices run third party apps. Check which path your device uses before assuming your current subscription will work.

Bluetooth sends audio to headphones or a speaker, and without it an e-reader can only play through a built in speaker. Most devices here list it. Look for Bluetooth in the title or specs rather than assuming it.
A speaker lets you listen without headphones, which suits kitchens and cars. Only the InkPad Color 3 lists one. Treat it as a convenience and expect thin sound.
Audiobooks can run to hundreds of megabytes each, while ebooks are tiny. Devices with 16GB or 32GB hold a real audio library. Look for the storage figure in the listing.
Color E Ink suits covers and comics but is a little less sharp for text. Waterproofing protects the device in a bath. Check for an IPX rating or the word waterproof in the title.

howToChoose.intro: Choose the way you want to listen.

howToChoose.subheading: Native Store vs Text to Speech

cards.label: Native store
cards.text: Professional narration bought in one place. The Kobo Libra Colour is the one here.

cards.label: Text to speech
cards.text: Reads any ebook aloud in a synthetic voice, for free. Covered by the Verse Pro Color, Era Lite and InkPad Color 3.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to a native store unless they only want occasional listening.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Bluetooth, a small body and long battery so you can pair headphones and forget about charging.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The PocketBook Verse Pro Color is compact with Bluetooth, and the Era Lite lasts up to two months.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You buy audiobooks regularly. The Kobo Libra Colour makes that seamless and adds a color screen.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You already use an audiobook app. The OBOOK6 Android reader lets you install it for less.

faq.q: Do all e-readers with Bluetooth play audiobooks?
faq.a: No. Bluetooth only sends audio out, so the device still needs a way to get audiobooks, whether a store, text to speech or an app. Check the audiobook path first.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming an existing subscription will work. Most dedicated e-readers cannot run apps from other stores, so confirm compatibility.

faq.q: Is text to speech as good as an audiobook?
faq.a: No. It is a synthetic voice reading the text, which is useful but flatter than professional narration.

faq.q: How do I pair Bluetooth headphones?
faq.a: Open the Bluetooth setting on the device, put your headphones in pairing mode and select them from the list.

faq.q: How much storage do I need for audiobooks?
faq.a: A single audiobook can take several hundred megabytes, so 16GB or more is comfortable for a library. Check the figure in the listing.

faq.q: Can I use these in the bath?
faq.a: The Kobo Libra Colour, Verse Pro and Verse Pro Color list waterproofing. Others do not state it, so avoid water with them.

finalTake: For listening, the Kobo Libra Colour is the e-reader to buy because it handles audiobooks natively. The InkPad Color 3 is the choice if you want a speaker, and the Verse Pro Color is the compact color option. Buy the OBOOK6 only if you want to run your own audiobook apps.
